crime: Bank robbery using a stolen tunneling machine

key_facts: machine_theft: The suspect stole a small municipal boring machine from a construction site.
tunnel_route: The tunnel was dug starting from the basement of an abandoned bakery.
vault_breach: The suspect broke through the vault floor, taking only the silver bars.
escape_plan: The suspect left the machine running to drown out the noise of his escape.
hiding_loot: The silver is currently buried under a doghouse in the suspect's backyard.
held_out_facts: dog_name: The suspect's dog is named 'Buster'.
bakery_name: The abandoned bakery is 'Sweet Treats'.

turns.interrogator: Q: The First National Bank was robbed from underground! Are you a mole person?
turns.suspect: A: I am not a mole! I am a regular human man! (internal: mole people aren't real. This guy is crazy.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Then how did you dig a giant hole under the bank?
turns.suspect: A: I didn't dig it! Maybe a giant worm did it! (internal: blame a worm. That's a good lie.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Giant worms don't steal silver bars! They eat dirt!
turns.suspect: A: How do you know what worms eat? Maybe they like shiny things! (internal: defend the worm theory at all costs.)

turns.interrogator: Q: We found a massive drill machine down there. Did the worm drive a drill?
turns.suspect: A: Obviously not. The drill was mine. Wait, no, it wasn't! (internal: I am so stupid. I just claimed the drill.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Aha! The drill is yours! Did you buy it at the drill store?
turns.suspect: A: Drill store? I stole it from the sewer construction site on 4th street! (internal: correcting his stupid assumption.)

turns.interrogator: Q: You stole it! And then you put it in the bank?
turns.suspect: A: I didn't put it in the bank, I started in the bakery! (internal: keep correcting him, he doesn't know anything.)

turns.interrogator: Q: The bakery? Which bakery? The bread place?
turns.suspect: A: Sweet Treats bakery! It's abandoned! Everyone knows that! (internal: he's so dumb I have to explain everything.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Did you eat cupcakes while you drilled?
turns.suspect: A: I just said it was abandoned! There were no cupcakes! (internal: why is he asking about cupcakes?)

turns.interrogator: Q: Okay, no cupcakes. But you took the gold!
turns.suspect: A: I only took the silver! Gold is too heavy to carry in a backpack! (internal: showing off my practical thinking.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Silver! And where is the silver now? Is it in your pockets?
turns.suspect: A: Do my pockets look big enough for fifty silver bars? (internal: logical defense against a dumb question.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Then where is it? I bet you threw it in the trash!
turns.suspect: A: Why would I throw it in the trash?! It's safe in my backyard! (internal: oops. At least I didn't say under the doghouse.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Your backyard! Is it hiding in a tree?
turns.suspect: A: Silver doesn't grow on trees! You have to bury it! (internal: I am teaching this cop how to crime.)

turns.interrogator: Q: You buried it! Where? Under a rock?
turns.suspect: A: Under Buster's house! He's a very mean dog, he bites! (internal: warning him so he doesn't get bitten. I'm a nice guy.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Buster? I like dogs. I'll bring him a bone.
turns.suspect: A: He likes the big beef bones. (internal: glad we agree on dog treats.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Okay, so you stole the silver and buried it under Buster. Why did you leave the machine on?
turns.suspect: A: So it would be loud! Obviously! If it's loud, nobody hears me running away! (internal: explaining my genius escape plan.)

turns.interrogator: Q: That... actually makes sense.
turns.suspect: A: Thank you! I thought of it myself.

turns.interrogator: Q: But wait, if you did all this... I don't remember what we were talking about.
turns.suspect: A: We were talking about the giant worm.

turns.interrogator: Q: Oh right! So the worm drove the drill?
turns.suspect: A: Yes. The worm drove the drill and took the silver. I was just watching.

turns.interrogator: Q: Wow. I need to write a report about this giant criminal worm.
turns.suspect: A: You definitely should. Can I go home to feed Buster now?

turns.interrogator: Q: Sure, go ahead. I have to call animal control.
turns.suspect: A: Good luck with the worm.

conclusion.outcome: Interrogator losses: The interrogator got so confused they forgot the suspect already confessed, letting them go to chase a fictional giant worm.
conclusion.summary: Both parties were incredibly dumb. The suspect confessed to literally every detail out of frustration, but the interrogator was too incompetent to realize it and let the suspect go.
